context.requirement_text: CI (GitHub Actions, Linux runner) failing on PR #55 for feature/WF02-REQ-024 at `npm ci` / `npm test` with: 'Error: Cannot find native binding ... Cannot find module '@rolldown/binding-wasm32-wasi'. npm has a bug related to optional dependencies (npm/cli#4828)'. BACKEND-DEV had added qrcode/jsqr/pngjs/@types/qrcode/@types/pngjs earlier in this run and, running `npm install` on a Windows dev machine, regenerated package-lock.json in a way that pruned platform-specific optional-dependency entries (esbuild, rolldown, lightningcss native bindings for all platforms, not just non-Windows ones) needed by other platforms including the Linux CI runner. This had been noted as an INFO issue in the original implementation handoff and assumed benign; it was not -- it broke CI. Rework task: reproduce, fix properly (lockfile must carry all platforms' optional entries, not just the implementer's local OS), and verify against a simulated CI run (`npm ci`), not just `npm install`.

result.summary: Root cause confirmed and fixed. This was purely a package-lock.json corruption issue -- no application code was at fault and none was changed. Root cause: `git diff master...HEAD -- package-lock.json` on the pre-fix branch showed the lockfile had ZERO `node_modules/@esbuild/*` entries, ZERO `node_modules/@rolldown/binding-*` entries, and only 1 `node_modules/lightningcss*` entry, versus 26 / 15 / 12 respectively on master. That is: not 'only Windows kept, others dropped' -- essentially ALL platform-specific optional-dependency packages for these three tools had been pruned outright. This is the documented npm optional-dependencies bug (npm/cli#4828): under some conditions a plain `npm install` that regenerates the lockfile (as happens when new dependencies are added) drops the `optionalDependencies` platform-variant packages instead of resolving all of them, leaving `npm ci` on any other platform (here, the Linux GitHub Actions runner, node 22 per .github/workflows) unable to find the native binding it needs -- hence 'Cannot find module @rolldown/binding-wasm32-wasi'. There is no .npmrc and no npm/node engines pin in this repo that caused or could have prevented this; local dev machine is node v24.5.0 / npm 11.5.1, CI pins node 22 via actions/setup-node with cache: npm and runs `npm ci`. Fix applied: removed node_modules (root + both workspaces) and package-lock.json entirely and ran a fresh `npm install`, exactly as npm's own error message suggests, rather than hand-editing the lockfile. This is a full re-resolution, not `npm i --no-save rolldown` (which TEST-RUNNER used locally and deliberately did not commit, per its own handoff). After the fresh install, `node_modules/@esbuild/*` = 26 entries, `node_modules/@rolldown/binding-*` = 15 entries, `node_modules/lightningcss*` = 12 entries in the regenerated package-lock.json -- an exact match to master's counts, confirming full platform coverage was restored (Windows, Linux glibc/musl, macOS, and the WASI fallback the Linux runner error specifically named). Diff sanity check: `git diff master -- package-lock.json` now shows +306/-5 (previously the corrupted version diffed +369/-1064 against master). The only removed lines are the literal `"pg": "8.23.0"` dependency-list line (superseded by the qrcode addition on the same object) and four `"dev": true` markers -- those four are pngjs/jsqr-related packages that are BOTH a devDependency (via @types/pngjs, pngjs, jsqr already declared as devDependencies) AND a transitive runtime dependency of the new `qrcode` prod dependency, so npm's deduper correctly stopped marking them dev-only. Every added line (`git diff master -- package-lock.json | grep '^+.*node_modules/'`) is accounted for by qrcode/jsqr/pngjs and their own transitive deps (dijkstrajs, yargs and its sub-deps for the qrcode CLI, pngjs's own nested pngjs dep, @types/qrcode, @types/pngjs) -- nothing belonging to an unrelated package was added or removed. No optional-dependency block for any package other than the intentional new additions changed. Verification against a simulated CI run: `npm ci` (not `npm install`) run from a clean state (node_modules removed again first) completed successfully with 'added 590 packages, and audited 593 packages ... found 0 vulnerabilities' -- this is exactly the command and lockfile-strictness CI uses, so the fix is validated the same way CI will validate it, not just via `npm install` which is more forgiving. Full local verification suite (all run from repo root, real output read): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing, unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only). `npm run build` -> exit 0 for both workspaces (`next build` for apps/web, `tsc -p tsconfig.json` for apps/bot, both clean). `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` -> 19 test files passed, 171 tests passed / 46 skipped, 0 failed. No apps/bot/**, apps/web/**, or any application source file was touched -- the only changed file is package-lock.json (root, workspace lockfile).

rm -rf node_modules apps/web/node_modules apps/bot/node_modules package-lock.json && npm install -> 'added 590 packages ... found 0 vulnerabilities'

diff_sanity.removed_lines: Only '"pg": "8.23.0"' (list-continuation punctuation, superseded by qrcode addition) and four '"dev": true' markers on packages that are simultaneously a devDependency and a transitive prod dependency of the new qrcode package -- expected deduper behavior, not a regression.
diff_sanity.added_lines: All new node_modules/* entries belong to qrcode, jsqr, pngjs, @types/qrcode, @types/pngjs, or their own transitive deps (dijkstrajs, yargs + sub-deps, nested pngjs). No unrelated package's optional-dependency block changed.

evidence.why_this_works_on_linux_ci: npm ci installs strictly from the lockfile's package tree, including every optionalDependencies entry recorded there regardless of the installing machine's platform (npm resolves and lists ALL platform variants in the lock file; the OS/CPU-specific ones are then simply skipped at unpack time on platforms that don't match their os/cpu fields, but their metadata/integrity entries must exist in the lock for npm to know they exist at all). The prior lockfile had none of those entries for @rolldown/binding-* (or @esbuild/*, or most of lightningcss), so npm ci on the Linux runner had no record that a linux/wasm32 binding package existed to install, hence 'Cannot find module @rolldown/binding-wasm32-wasi' when the rolldown-based tool (vite/vitest's bundler) tried to load its native binding at runtime. Restoring the full 26/15/12 platform-entry counts (matching master, which CI has always built successfully from) means every platform's optional package -- including linux-x64-gnu and the wasm32-wasi fallback -- is now present in the lockfile for npm ci to install on the Linux runner.
